title: Unserved combination survives a 2026 skeptic sweep; nearest partial is an agent IFC runtime (nucleus), not a middle-tier server
summary: Skeptic search (web, 3 queries; GitHub repo search, 7 queries pushed>=2026-06; repo/code inspection of 3 candidates) found no 2026 server/gateway combining PQ TLS + capability authz + machine-checked or DST claims + lean single binary. Nearest partials: coproduct-opensource/nucleus (MIT, created 2026-01-31, v2.7.0 2026-10-08) = agent tool-proxy with an IFC permission lattice backed by Lean 4 (195 .lean files) + Kani, SPIFFE identity, Firecracker pods, MCP, but >100 workspace crates and not a front proxy; Rullst (MIT, 2026-05-25) full-stack framework with Kani/Miri scopes + Verus pilot, TLS delegated to Caddy, 'capability' = feature modules; agentgateway v1.6.0 (2026-10-02) / v1.7.0-alpha.1 (2026-10-21): aws-lc-rs 1.18 (PQ via rustls default), CEL authz, MCP/A2A, zero code-search hits for cedar/kani/verus/turmoil/madsim.
specifics: verdict=unchanged (conjunction) / up on underclaim. numbers_checked: candidates_meeting_all_4=0 (gh search 2026-10-25); nucleus lean files=195; agentgateway latest=v1.7.0-alpha.1 2026-10-21. Decision R-GAP-1 unchanged; positioning must cite nucleus as prior art for machine-checked agent authz lattices.
overclaim_risk: Absence over GitHub search + 3 inspections; closed products and non-English repos unchecked; code search can return 0 for unindexed repos.
underclaim_risk: Machine-checked authz for agents (nucleus) and PQ-default gateways (agentgateway) already exist separately; the gap is the conjunction plus leanness, narrower than 'unserved'.

title: FIPS pin recomputed from CMVP: #5298/#5314 = AWS-LC FIPS 3.1.0 with ML-KEM approved, no ML-DSA; exact crate = aws-lc-fips-sys =0.13.11 (aws-lc-rs version is not the lever)

Approved: ML-KEM KeyGen/EncapDecap (512/768/1024), EdDSA, HKDF, TLS 1.2/1.3 KDF; NOT ML-DSA, NOT SLH-DSA; X25519 absent from boundary. #5429 (2026-07-20, sunset 2029-08-13) is AWS-LC FIPS 2.0.0 dynamic, no ML-KEM (not a 4.0 cert). MIP: AWS-LC 4 dyn+static 'Comment Resolution - Lab (10/22/2026)'; AWS-LC 5 'Pending Review (10/5/2026)'. Crate map: aws-lc-fips-sys 0.13.11 (2026-01-14) vendors AWSLC_VERSION_NUMBER_STRING 3.1.0; 6 sampled fipsmodule files sha256-identical to tag AWS-LC-FIPS-3.1.0; vcs dirty=true and no aws-lc-rs git tag for 0.13.11. 0.13.12 -> FIPS-3.2.0; 0.13.13/14 -> 3.3.0; 0.13.15-17 -> commits ahead of 3.3.0; 0.13.8-10 -> 4 commits before 3.1.0. aws-lc-rs 1.15.2..1.17.0 all require aws-lc-fips-sys ^0.13.1, 1.18.0 requires ^0.14.0.

title: PQ handshake cost recomputed from raw logs: rustls +12.5..15.0% (the +17.5% best trial is not in any log), Envoy +24-25%, OpenSSL +29..74%
summary: Recomputed from state/raw/round-002/w02/out and out2 logs (12 trial pairs). rustls (hellotls): 141.7->159.3 us (+12.5%), 254.8->292.9 (+15.0%); the reported 'best trial 123.4->145.0 (+17.5%)' appears in no raw log (unreproducible). Envoy/BoringSSL: 170.8->211.9 (+24.0%), 121.1->151.7 (+25.3%). Caddy/Go: +42.8%, +39.0%. nginx/OpenSSL 3.5: +31.9%, +74.2% (out2), +55.5% (auto); HAProxy/OpenSSL: +30.3%, +28.6%, +31.6% (mc4096). Absolute X25519 cost: Envoy's best (121.1) is below rustls's best logged (141.7); rustls~Envoy, both ~1.7x below OpenSSL servers (246/141). Trial-to-trial spread up to 1.8x (rustls 141.7 vs 254.8) from host contention; trials were not interleaved. Relative-delta ordering rustls < Envoy < OpenSSL holds in every trial pair; 'rustls cheapest in absolute CPU' does not.
specifics: Band (per-server min..max relative delta): rustls 12.5-15.0% (n=2), Envoy 24.0-25.3% (n=2), HAProxy 28.6-31.6% (n=3), nginx 31.9-74.2% (n=3), Caddy 39.0-42.8% (n=2). Abs delta: rustls +17.7..+38.1 us; OpenSSL +74..+251 us. Re-run spike: interleaved ABBA trials, 5 reps, pinned isolated cores, report median + IQR.
overclaim_risk: n=2-3 per server on a contended laptop; non-interleaved; best-trial selection without a log.
underclaim_risk: All bands still show hybrid ML-KEM is cheap at household scale (<40 us per handshake on rustls).

numbers_checked.claim: rustls ~2x cheaper than OpenSSL at X25519 and cheapest overall

decision_change: none (TLS stack choice not driven by this delta); downgrade wording in BENCH_PLAN

title: CRS clause evidence audit: C1, C6, C8 rested on <=2 instances (now 3+); C4 rests on spec text only; key-epoch transitions are an uncovered class
summary: Instance count per clause from r2 explorer-10 counterexamples, plus third instances fetched from cveawg/KEV/vendor advisories. C1 provenance: GnuTLS CVE-2020-13777 + AWS ALB rotation, THIRD Apache Superset CVE-2023-27524 (default SECRET_KEY forges server-issued sessions; CISA KEV 2024-01-08). C2 scope: >=4 (nginx CVE-2025-23419, Apache CVE-2025-23048, Fastly, Cloudflare). C3 key completeness: >=3 (cache deception multi-vendor, 16 curl reuse CVEs in 2026, Next.js CVE-2026-44572). C4 freshness: RFC 8446 §8 / RFC 9001 §9.2 + idempotency draft; no 0-RTT replay CVE found; adjacent mbedTLS CVE-2026-73096 (2026-07-07, early data silently dropped via forged EndOfEarlyData). C5 epoch: session fixation + curl CVE-2016-5419 + Hebrok 2025, THIRD PostgreSQL CVE-2026-14666 (2026-08-13, cached RLS policy survives role change). C6 failure atomicity: was effectively one codebase (PyJWT CVE-2026-48524 + incomplete fix CVE-2026-101917); SECOND RabbitMQ CVE-2026-67409 (2026-09-25, non-200 JWKS response destroys signing keys -> auth DoS); THIRD libjwt commit 22a089aa. C7: XFF (Litestar, Lemmy), JWKS kid, hashDoS + client-side rustls RUSTSEC-2026-0349 (unauthenticated ServerHello cached group downgrades later connections). C8: HPACK/HEIST + coalescing draft, THIRD/FOURTH Tomcat CVE-2024-52317 (2024-11-18) and CVE-2026-101356 (2026-10-20) HTTP/2 request/response mix-up between users via object recycling. Counterexample to completeness: connection-level key-epoch transitions (rustls RUSTSEC-2026-0285 handshake messages accepted across encryption levels, 2026-09-14; mbedTLS CVE-2026-73096) are not stated by any clause.
specifics: Revisions: C8 add 'pooled/recycled request and response objects are reset and never carry data across principals (Tomcat CVE-2024-52317/2026-101356)'. C5 add 'C5b: at every TLS/QUIC key or encryption-level change, buffered unprocessed input is empty or the connection aborts' (oracle: inject trailing bytes after ClientHello/Finished in same record -> expect alert). C6 oracle: JWKS fetch returning 500/404/HTML keeps last-good keys (RabbitMQ CVE-2026-67409 replay). C1 oracle: startup refuses known-default/placeholder secrets (Superset pattern). C4 grade C-observed (spec-derived).
overclaim_risk: Mapping incidents to clauses is judgement; Tomcat mix-ups are object-recycling bugs that C8's wording only loosely covers; mbedTLS CVE id not yet in cveawg (vendor advisory only).
underclaim_risk: Each clause now has >=3 independent instances except C4, so the invariant is incident-grounded, not speculative.
verdict: up (C1/C6/C8 grounded) / down (C4 spec-only; completeness gap at key-epoch)

title: Cedar TCB at 301bdd2 (main HEAD 2026-10-23): kernel + Lean compiler (native_decide on SymCC path) + cvc5 for analysis verdicts; Rust tied by DRT, parsers by round-trip PBT only
summary: cedar-spec main == 301bdd22df13 (2026-10-23), lean-toolchain v4.35.0. native_decide: 10 in proof path (Cedar/Data/Int64.lean x2: toInt_nonneg_of_ge_zero / toInt_neg_of_not_ge_zero via (0:Int64).toInt=0; Cedar/Thm/SymCC/Data/Ext.lean x8: msPerDay literal and tdiv bounds) + 16 in UnitTest. The Int64 lemmas are used by Thm/SymCC/{Decoder, Term/TypeOf, Data, Tactics, Concretizer/WF,Lit,Same, Term/PE, Interpretation, Term/Interpret/Basic}, so SymCC soundness/completeness theorems very likely depend on Lean.ofReduceBool; core authz theorems do not import these files by grep (likely axiom-clean, unverified). cvc5 is the only supported solver (Cedar/SymCC/Solver.lean) and is trusted for verify* verdicts. partial def: 1 in Cedar/ (SymCC/Decoder), 40 in CedarProto/ (protobuf decode on the DRT/FFI path). DRT: 84 fuzz targets in cedar-drt/fuzz/fuzz_targets (32 'drt'-named, 12 'pbt'); README table stale (41 rows: 18 DRT, 23 PBT). Policy/schema parsers are covered only by round-trip PBT (outside the Lean model). Public CI builds the fuzz crate and runs cargo test; no time-budgeted cargo fuzz run and no cron in public workflows.
specifics: TCB for AEGIS use of Cedar authorizer: Lean kernel (authz theorems) + cedar-policy Rust evaluator (trusted, DRT-tested) + Cedar parser (trusted, PBT-tested). If AEGIS uses SymCC policy analysis in CI: add Lean compiler/runtime (native_decide) + cvc5. Spike: `lake env lean` with `#print axioms Cedar.Thm.forbid_trumps_permit` and `#print axioms Cedar.Thm.verifyNeverErrors_is_sound` (needs Lean toolchain, no Mathlib).
overclaim_risk: Axiom dependence inferred by grep, not #print axioms; DRT may run internally at AWS beyond public CI.
underclaim_risk: native_decide uses are closed literal computations, trivially replaceable; the TCB growth is real but low-risk.

title: Wasmtime exposure as a per-year escape RATE: minimal config M0 had 12 exploitable escapes 2021-2026 (2.0/yr, 95% CI 1.0-3.5), 1 since 2024; the 9% share is a denominator artifact
summary: Recomputed from round-002 07-data/classified.json (81 GHSAs, snapshot 2026-10-25, not re-pulled). Advisories per year: 2021 4, 2022 8, 2023 4, 2024 4, 2025 4, 2026 57 (audit sprint). Exploitable sandbox escapes hitting M0 (x86_64 Cranelift core wasm): 2021 2, 2022 5, 2023 4, 2024 0, 2025 0, 2026 1 (GHSA-897f-g5gm-fmxm) [+2 2026 knob-only non-exploitable]. Total 12 in ~5.8 y = ~2.0/yr (Poisson 95% CI 1.03-3.49); 2024-2026: 1 in 2.8 y (0.36/yr, CI 0.01-2.0). M1 (+P2 components) adds 2 escapes in 2026 (string transcoding OOB), M2 (+wasi-fs) adds 2 more (2026). Guest-triggerable share for M0 per year (Wilson 95%): 2024 2/4 (0.15-0.85), 2025 0/4 (0-0.49), 2026 4/57 (0.03-0.17). The '6/65 = 9%' share for 2024-26 is driven by 57 advisories in 2026 inflating the denominator; share is not exposure.
specifics: Decision input for R-ISO-1: use 'M0 exploitable escapes per year' with band 0.36-2.0/yr (recent vs long-run) instead of advisory share; assume >=1 critical escape per ~1-3 years for any Wasm host, so Wasm cannot be the sole boundary for third-party code (pair with process/seccomp/Landlock).
overclaim_risk: Classification inherited from r2 hand tags (+-3-5 advisories); n tiny per year; 2026 audit sprint changes discovery rate, so rates are not stationary.
underclaim_risk: Long-run 2.0/yr M0 escape rate (2021-23 cluster in core Cranelift/reftypes/SIMD) is much higher than the 2024-26 share suggests.
decision_change: R-ISO-1 rationale changes to rate-based; decision (Wasm only with OS sandbox defense-in-depth for third-party code) unchanged
